title: Trace transport and compare developmental origins
introduction: Choose a map, then select a structure. Transport arrows show anatomical order; developmental cards compare contributors and are not a sequence of one structure turning into the next.

maps.label: Sperm transport
maps.title: From producing epithelium to the outflow route

steps.label: Seminiferous tubule
steps.detail: Germ cells develop within Sertoli-cell support; spermiation releases sperm into the lumen. This is the producing epithelium, not an epididymal lining.

steps.label: Straight tubule and rete testis
steps.detail: Straight tubules lead to the rete channels in the mediastinal region. The local lining differs from the germ-cell-rich seminiferous epithelium.

steps.label: Efferent ductules
steps.detail: Connect the rete with the epididymal duct. Compare ciliated and nonciliated absorptive populations and their uneven luminal border.

steps.label: Epididymal duct
steps.detail: A highly coiled conducting system with a pseudostratified lining. Stereocilia are long microvilli. Repeated profiles need not be separate ducts.

steps.label: Ductus deferens
steps.detail: The folded mucosa is surrounded by a substantial muscular wall. Compare the epithelial lining with the endothelium of adjacent vessels.

steps.label: Ejaculatory duct
steps.detail: The distal deferent route joins the seminal-vesicle duct. Secretions enter the transport pathway; sperm do not normally traverse the seminal-vesicle gland.

steps.label: Urethra
steps.detail: The ejaculatory route empties into the prostatic urethra. Prostatic secretions also enter through gland ducts. Regional epithelial types require their own anatomical context.

references.title: Southern Illinois University — reproductive tract overview

maps.limit: A schematic route, not a scale drawing, transport-rate simulation or claim that all connections occur in one slide.

maps.label: Developmental contributors
maps.title: Keep epithelial origin and tissue interactions distinct

steps.label: Selected mesonephric tubules
steps.detail: Contribute to the efferent ductules. Distinguish these tubules from the mesonephric duct itself.

steps.label: Mesonephric duct epithelium
steps.detail: Contributes to the epididymal and deferent duct system; seminal vesicles develop as outgrowths of its lower region.

steps.label: Urogenital-sinus epithelium
steps.detail: Provides the prostatic epithelial budding system, followed by branching, canalization and differentiation.

steps.label: Surrounding mesenchyme
steps.detail: Supplies a developmental signalling and supporting-tissue context. An epithelial origin does not assign the same origin to muscle, vessels and every other organ component.

steps.label: Gonadal supporting-cell programme
steps.detail: Cord organization and germ-cell support are part of gonadal development, distinct from identifying a duct derivative.
